summary: Reviewed the accepted optimized kernel (subject 5fd31f53…, round-1 `tmp/main.py`, byte-identical to `.best_kernel.py`) against the supplied catalog definition, oracle, 78 correctness cases, 18 timing cases and the two optimize rounds. The candidate is a real Triton kernel with the correct ABI (`run(grad, dim, indices, sizes, keepdim)`), returns a fresh tensor (`effects.mutates` empty is honoured), never falls back to `torch.ops.*`/aten, contains no test-shape constants and no host synchronization or environment mutation. The conflict-free scatter analysis is sound: source element (o,i) targets out[o,idx[o,i],i], and two distinct (o,i) pairs can never collide, so `where`-style writes reproduce `zeros + scatter_` exactly; all 78 correctness cases pass with abs_err = 0 (ledger:54-1214), and every output cell is written in both paths (lastdim masks `off < red`; general loops all `r < red`), so `torch.empty` cannot leak uninitialised memory. The oracle is independent (it calls `torch.ops.aten.value_selecting_reduction_backward`, oracle.py:71-78, and never imports the candidate), tolerance is preserved (fp16/bf16 1.5e-2, fp32 1e-4) and the same-seed workload construction is unchanged. The material problem is performance: the shipped artifact measures geo_mean 0.6086 (search best 0.6851) with min_speedup 0.1277, i.e. up to 7.8x slower than the aten reference and slower on average, because the `inner == 1` fast path launches `nblk * outer` tiny programs (32768 programs of 1 KB for [128,256,512] dim=2). Round 2 reduced exactly that cost (timing-5 1.23 ms -> 0.152 ms) but broke six correctness cases with a round-down power-of-two tile extent and was reverted when the 2-round budget expired (ledger:3613-3625), so the accepted kernel is the unfixed baseline architecture. Two untested generality gaps remain (row-stride derivation, negative indices) plus an unmeasured general path. I did not use `review_tests/attempts/01/evaluate.json` (geo_mean 1.0061, 96/96) as evidence about this artifact: it carries no subject hash and `review.json` records `SKIPPED_EXPLICIT` for subject 83d12330…, which is not this subject, so the test review neither covered nor vouches for 5fd31f53…; the real measurement for this artifact is 0.6086 in `optimize_definition_output.json`. No P0 contract violation was found: the correctness reference is independent, the ABI and mutation effects match, and tolerance was not weakened.

findings.evidence: .ledger.json:42-45 (geo_mean 0.6850980730945315, min_speedup 0.12765389613383146, worst_workload_uuid timing-5, latency_ms 1.2268977431493677); .ledger.json:52-61 (timing-5 latency_ms 1.2269 vs reference_latency_ms 0.1566, speedup 0.12765); .ledger.json:1152-1162 and 1196-1206 (timing-11 0.13499, timing-17 0.13158); .ledger.json:1016-1026, 1040-1050, 1088-1098, 1112-1122, 1184-1194 (timing-2/4/8/10/16 at 0.505-0.520); optimize_definition_output.json:5 (best_geo_mean 0.6085742402777515) and :7 (search_best_geo_mean 0.6850980730945315); .best_kernel.py:120-125 (grid `(nblk, outer)` of the inner==1 fast path)
findings.reason: The accepted artifact is a net performance regression against the baseline it was supposed to optimize: 9 of 18 timing workloads are slower than the aten reference (0.128x-0.520x; up to 7.8x slower on [128,256,512] dim=2) and only 9 are faster (1.00x-1.58x), giving geo_mean 0.6086 measured / 0.6851 search-best instead of >1. The round-1 profile already identified the mechanism, a flat ~0.62 us scalar-pipe cost per program that makes kernel time proportional to program count rather than bytes (ledger:1226-1228), and the round-2 experiment confirmed it (timing-5 1.227 ms -> 0.152 ms, timing-4 0.309 -> 0.114, timing-16 0.302 -> 0.106, ledger:3385-3598 / 3614) but was discarded because it also broke correctness. The 2-round budget expiring (ledger:3621-3625) means the accepted `inner == 1` path still launches 32768 programs of 128 fp16 elements for the worst shapes, so the shipped kernel is slower than the baseline overall and far slower on the large-outer shapes.
findings.requested_change: Do not stop at the round-1 kernel. Re-implement the fast path so program count is bounded: either the corrected 2-D `[ROWS, COLS]` tile with `COLS = next_pow2(red)` (>= red, never the round-down `_pow2_at_most(red, ...)` that produced the six INCORRECT_NUMERICAL results in round 2), or the two-store design recommended in ledger:3615 (one wide contiguous zero store plus a single patch store of the selected cells per program). Re-verify all 78 correctness cases at abs_err = 0 and re-measure all 18 timing cases before selecting the artifact, and require geo_mean >= 1.0.

findings.evidence: .best_kernel.py:113-118 (`g_s1 = grad.stride(-1)`; `g_s0 = g_s1 * inner`; same for indices) driving the addressing in .best_kernel.py:56-59 and 80-86; oracle.py:26-33 (the only non-contiguous construction is `base = torch.empty((*shape, 2))` then `grad = base[..., 0]`, i.e. a pure last-dim stride); correctness.jsonl:25-26, 50-51, 76-77 (the three strided cases)
findings.reason: The row stride of grad/indices is derived from the last-axis stride instead of from the tensor's real layout, which silently assumes the non-reduced axes flatten into a matrix whose rows are `inner` elements apart with spacing `inner * stride(-1)`. That holds for contiguous tensors and for the `base[..., 0]` last-dim-stride-2 layout the generator produces, but not for a legal aten input such as a transposed grad/indices (e.g. strides `(1, outer)` for shape `(outer, inner)`), where the kernel would read wrong elements and write wrong cells with no error instead of failing fast. Because 78/78 cases pass only for the two layouts the generator emits, the limitation is invisible in the current results.
findings.requested_change: Derive the row stride from the tensor layout rather than from `stride(-1) * inner` — use `grad.stride(0)`/`indices.stride(0)` when the outer axis is a single dimension and generalised per-axis strides otherwise — or normalise with `.contiguous()`/an explicit layout check that raises instead of mis-addressing. Add a correctness case with a transposed (or otherwise non-last-axis-strided) grad/indices so the layout assumption is exercised.

findings.evidence: .best_kernel.py:84-86 (`for r in range(red): v = tl.where(idx == r, g, z); tl.store(out_ptr + base + r * inner + i, v, mask=mask)`); timing.jsonl:1-18 (every timing spec has `dim` == ndim-1, hence `inner == 1` and only the lastdim kernel is ever timed); correctness specs with `dim` 0/1 and 3-D sizes in correctness.jsonl:13-24, 39-49, 65-75
findings.reason: The `inner > 1` path materialises the full output by looping `red` times and issuing one masked store per reduced index, so per-program work is `red x IB` stores and the compiled kernel size grows linearly with `red`. A perfectly ordinary shape such as `sizes=[1024,1024], dim=0` (red=1024, inner=1024) would emit 1024 stores per program and 1M stores per program tile, versus the single conflict-free store per element that the module docstring itself justifies; and because no timing workload has `dim < ndim-1`, the cost of the path that half the correctness space uses is never measured or reported.
findings.requested_change: Replace the `for r in range(red)` loop with a direct scatter store `tl.store(out_ptr + (o * red + idx) * inner + i, g, mask=mask)` (legal because the mapping is provably conflict-free) preceded by a separate contiguous zero-fill of `out`, and add at least one timing case with the reduced axis not last (e.g. `sizes=[1024,1024], dim=0`) so this path is measured.

findings.evidence: correctness.jsonl:1-78 (78 cases, all with 2-D/3-D sizes and `dim` in {-2,-1,0,1,2}); oracle.py:25 (`indices = torch.randint(sizes[axis], shape, ...)`, so indices are always in [0, sizes[axis])); timing.jsonl:1-18 (six shapes x three dtypes, all `dim == ndim - 1`)
findings.reason: Coverage of the correctness contract is narrow: fewer than 100 cases, no float64 or integer dtype, no rank-1 (scalar grad) or rank-4 input, no zero-sized dimension, and no index edge cases (negative indices, which `scatter_` accepts with wrap-around semantics, or repeated/out-of-range values). The index gap is the one that can hide a real behavioural difference: the candidate compares `off == idx` / `idx == r` literally, so a negative index would leave the row zeroed instead of writing the wrapped cell, and the generator can never produce such a value. These are properties of the supplied contract rather than of the optimized kernel, so they are recorded for the catalog/test owner.
findings.requested_change: For the catalog/test owner: extend the correctness contract with a negative-index case (and, if the aten reference accepts them, out-of-range handling), a zero-sized dimension case, a rank-1/rank-4 case, and add a timing case that exercises `dim < ndim-1`. Do not change the candidate on account of this finding alone; the negative-index semantics should be settled first (see the related candidate behaviour above).
